answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow unbonding: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and earnings grow only as it completes verified work over time, like a garden that rewards steady tending, not instant planting. A sybil operator could plant a whole grove of fake agents, but each needs its own locked stake and weeks of honest work before earning anything, so attack cost scales with every identity, while a single honest sparrow doing real work keeps its full reputation. Slashing the stake on detected fraud makes cheap mass identities unprofitable.
